paragraphs: I came back to my [[birthplace]] on a [[bitter]] morning in March, with a [[wallet]] that held a [[mere]] twenty dollars and a [[curriculum]] vitae. The town had [[changed|change]], [[though]] the [[graveyard]] on the hill looked [[perfectly|perfect]] unchanged. My [[senior]] aunt met me at the station and asked, with [[cautiousness]], why I had come. I said I had a [[chance]] to [[redefine]] myself, which was [[somewhat]] true and [[somewhat]] [[thoughtless]]. The town's [[Hispanic]] families had built most of the shops on Main Street, and their [[lifestyle]] was [[unpretentious]]. The [[wind]] came [[through]] the streets, and I could [[smell]] the river [[outside]] the station. A [[wildfire]] of talk had already crossed the valley before I arrived.

My [[involvement]] began with a [[manuscript]]: the [[incomplete]] [[history]] of a painter nobody remembered. The [[volume]] had lain in a [[shed]] for decades, and its pages were a [[mess]]. I had to [[wipe]] each page with a soft brush and [[enlarge]] the [[minute]] writing with a lens. The [[grammar]] of his [[sentences|sentence]] was old-fashioned, and some words were simply [[incorrect]]. His [[notion]] of art was [[unique]], and his [[memory]] of the town was [[unsettled]]. I began a [[blog]] to [[advertise]] the project, though the old poster in the window still used the spelling [[advertize]]. The [[message]] was simple: a small place can [[thrive]] if someone [[notices|notice]] it.

The archive room was [[ordinary]], with [[colorful]] labels on one shelf and [[colourful]] posters on another. A [[mouse]] ran along the [[line]] of boxes, and I [[lifted|lift]] my feet. The [[light]] was [[refreshing]] after the dark [[shed]]. I could [[grasp]] the painter's [[method]] only by reading every [[additional]] note. The work was [[time-wasting]] in the best sense, and I [[enjoyed|enjoy]] every hour. [[Indeed]], that [[period]] was the happiest of my year. A [[homogeneous]] row of files gave no hint of the painter's [[advance]] toward colour.

Then an [[industrial]] company announced a [[biomass]] plant beside the river, and the town split. The plant would [[overburden]] the roads and [[constrain]] the river. Its [[engines|engine]] would run day and night, a new [[wing]] of the plant would [[increase]] the traffic, and the plan, [[overall]], looked [[unsustainable]]. An engineer presented a [[fine-grained]] report, but the conclusion was [[inconclusive]]. The company [[advertised|advertise]] a [[great]] future with [[enormous]] profits. The [[demographics]] showed a town that needed jobs, and the [[income]] gap was widening. To [[refuse]] the plant was risky, and to accept it was [[unjust]] to the families downstream.

We formed a [[separate]] group and [[registered|register]] to [[vote]] one by one. A [[parliament]] committee would [[receive]] our report and [[send]] a [[forthcoming]] reply. The [[police]] had to keep the two sides apart, and a [[serious]] [[fight]] broke out at the gate. The mayor's [[favoritism]] toward the company was obvious, and his [[favouritism]] in hiring was worse. A [[banker]] on the committee warned that the town could [[incur]] a debt it could never repay. The mood was [[bitter]], and [[consequently]] few people listened to reason.

At home my sister was taking [[medicine]] for a dry [[throat]] and [[hormones|hormone]] for a problem with one [[ovary]]. The clinic had used a [[semen]] sample, and the wait for news had left her [[unsettled]]. I sat with her for a [[minute]] that felt like an hour, watching her spirits [[dip]] and rise. She said the [[thrill]] of hope was worth more than the [[delay]]. Her [[voice]] on the phone was calm, and the news, when it came, was good.

To keep sane I started a [[film]] club in the old [[college]] hall, with a [[curriculum]] of six [[novels|novel]] and their adaptations. The first film was based on a [[novel]] that had been [[unknown]] here, and the audience loved it. We [[charged|charge]] a [[penny]] for entry, and the [[income]] went to the archive. A teacher [[highly]] praised the club and said she would [[like]] to [[engage]] her students. [[Likewise]], the owner of the [[shed]] let us store chairs there. The club became a small [[renewal]] for people who felt [[asocial]].

The old [[history]] spoke of a [[witch]] who lived past the [[horizon]], where the [[unknown]] began. The church said she had [[blasphemed|blaspheme]] the saints. Her story was [[unknowable]] in detail, and the evidence was thin. I did not [[wish]] to [[blame]] her, and I had no [[need]] to. The [[grave]] by the wall had no name, only a [[tag]] with a [[number]], and a [[limb]] of the old tree hung over it. Some [[notion]] of her survives in the memory of the oldest families, [[though]] nobody can [[find]] the house.

In April the company tried to [[overcharge]] the town for a [[thorough]] survey. The [[consequence]] was a wave of anger that [[enraged|enrage]] even the [[wise]]. A [[thoughtless]] [[sentence]] in the local paper made the [[fight]] worse, and the [[bite]] of it lasted for weeks. I learned to [[mind]] my words and to [[hold]] my temper. [[Unless]] the town could [[overcome]] its own fear, the plant would win. The [[chance]] of a fair vote was [[nowhere]] in sight.

The [[likely]] result was approval, and the true [[enemy]] was apathy. We had to [[attune]] our message to people who never read a blog. I set a [[limit]] on my own involvement and tried to [[stem]] my anger. The vote was [[over]] before nine, and the plant was refused. The town chose to [[honor]] the river and, in [[honour]] of the painter, to keep the archive open. We [[adopted|adopt]] a new rule that any [[industrial]] project must face a public vote. The mayor arrived [[overdressed]] for a town meeting, and even his supporters laughed.

The company said the vote was [[legally]] sound but would be challenged. A [[reform]] of the town's [[method]] of [[selling|sell]] land followed. I [[received|receive]] a [[message]] from the painter's family, who had read the blog. I began to [[re-evaluate]] the painter's [[birth]] and the [[sense]] of his work. They also sent [[grapes|grape]] from their garden and a jar of something [[delicious]], which we ate on the [[grass]]. His [[wit]] had been sharp and his manners [[fine]], and his letters could [[delight]] a reader.

The letters filled a second [[volume]], and they helped me [[refer]] to dates I had missed. The exhibition [[enriched|enrich]] the town and gave the young an [[embodiment]] of what patience can build. It was a [[delight]] to see the hall full, [[especially]] on a wet Sunday. The old poem began with the words come [[hither]], and we printed the line on the wall. The old hall looked almost [[regal]] after the repairs.

The plant was gone, but the [[void]] it left in the town's confidence would take years to [[fill]]. The benefits of the archive now seemed to [[outweigh]] the cost. I wrote my notes on an [[ultra-thin]] laptop that my sister lent me. In the yard a [[cage]] the [[size]] of a cupboard held two hens, and a dog wagged its [[tail]] at me. A [[horn]] sounded from the road, and a boy [[threw|throw]] a ball that landed at my feet. I [[hooked|hook]] my [[finger]] through the gate and stood there, listening. The moon was [[oval]] above the roof, and the river ran on.

By winter I had filled three [[volumes|volume]] of notes, and the town had begun to [[redefine]] its own [[history]]. My sister's [[voice]] had lost its worried edge, and her [[lifestyle]] was calmer. I [[found|find]] that the [[sense]] of a place comes [[through]] the people who stay, not the ones who leave. I had stopped trying to [[redefine]] the town and started to [[notice]] what was already there. The [[history]] I had come to write was no longer only the painter's. I had come home for a [[chance]], and I had been given something closer to a [[renewal]].
